newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Ukraine says no increased radiation at Chernobyl.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine says no increased radiation at Chernobyl.

text.p: No increases in radiation or temperature have been registered at the Chernobyl nuclear plant this week, a Ukrainian government official said on Wednesday.

"No radiation or temperature changes were registered," Yuri Kostenko, Ukraine's Minister for Nuclear Safety, told Reuters during a conference in Vienna, contradicting remarks made by Chernobyl officials on Tuesday.
"There was an increase in neutron activity. If this were a nuclear reaction it would have to be accompanied by a rise in temperature and radiation, but these factors were not measured," he said.

Officials at the station said on Tuesday there had been sharp increases in neutron activity inside the "sarcophagus", the protective casing erected after Chernobyl's fourth reactor exploded on April 26, 1986, sending a radioactive cloud over much of Europe.
Kostenko said his ministry had formed a "special group" to look into the incident, adding the registered increase in neutron activity could be due to faulty measuring equipment.

"We need to review our investigations inside the sarcophagus but we have no money. We are now in contact with the U.S. government," added the minister, who was attending the International Atomic Energy Agency's annual congress in Vienna.

Kostenko said Ukraine needed "some millions" of dollars to upgrade the measuring equipment inside the now-defunct reactor, 140 km (90 miles) north of Kiev. "We'll need two to three millions just to get started," he said.

The minister's remarks came shortly after the Finnish Centre for Radiation and Nuclear Safety quoted an unnamed Ukrainian nuclear safety director as saying radiation measurements taken manually inside the Chernobyl plant had shown nothing out of the ordinary.
